geology: Native metal in hydrothermal quartz veins, placers, and disseminated epithermal/orogenic deposits; often alloyed with silver.
extraction: Cyanide leach (CIL/CIP) then carbon adsorption or Merrill-Crowe zinc cementation; smelt to dore; Miller chlorination then Wohlwill electrorefining to fine gold.
notes: Free-milling gold. Carbon adsorption (CIL/CIP) is the default modern recovery; Merrill-Crowe used when silver is high. Dore is impure Au-Ag bullion.

geology: Naturally occurring gold-silver alloy (20-55% Ag) in epithermal vein systems; a primary source of byproduct silver in gold ores.
extraction: Cyanidation; Merrill-Crowe favored due to high silver load; smelt to dore; parting / electrorefining splits Au and Ag.
notes: High silver content overloads carbon-stripping circuits, so Merrill-Crowe zinc cementation is preferred over carbon adsorption. Cross-links gold and silver commodities.

geology: Gold antimonide (pyrite group), ~44.7% Au / 55.3% Sb; forms in post-gold antimony mineralization, e.g. Darasun. Contains no silver.
extraction: Roast to volatilize/oxidize antimony, then cyanidation and carbon adsorption; smelt to dore and refine.
notes: Antimony must be removed (roasting) before cyanidation; antimony reports as a byproduct off-gas/oxide stream.

geology: Submicroscopic/invisible gold finely disseminated and encapsulated within arsenopyrite; direct cyanidation fails without oxidative pretreatment.
extraction: Oxidative pretreatment (pressure oxidation OR bio-oxidation OR roasting) to destroy the sulfide lattice and liberate gold; then cyanidation, CIL/carbon adsorption, dore, refining.
notes: Core refractory-gold gameplay branch. Three competing pretreatments: Roasting (As to As2O3, S to SO2), POX (autoclave 1-3h, up to 99.5% recovery), BioOxidation (bacterial, cheap but slow, ~2% lower recovery). Arsenic is the key hazardous byproduct.

geology: Fine gold encapsulated in pyrite; refractory to direct cyanidation; common in sulfidic orogenic/Carlin-type ores.
extraction: Pressure oxidation / bio-oxidation / roasting to break down pyrite; then cyanidation, CIL/carbon adsorption, dore, refining.
notes: Refractory-gold branch. Same POX/BIOX/Roast fork as arsenopyrite; sulfur reports as SO2 (roasting) or sulfuric acid (POX/BIOX). Alternate pretreatment stages are PressureOxidation or Roasting.

geology: Silver sulfide; argentite is the cubic high-temperature form, acanthite the monoclinic form stable below 177C. Chief primary silver ore mineral, but most silver is byproduct of Pb/Zn/Cu ores.
intermediate: silver concentrate / Pb-Ag-Zn-Cu concentrate; or lead-smelter bullion
extraction: Primary: cyanidation then Merrill-Crowe to dore. Byproduct route: recovered in lead smelting, Parkes desilvering (zinc added, Ag-Zn crust skimmed), cupellation, then Moebius electrorefining.
notes: Silver is overwhelmingly byproduct-driven from Pb/Zn/Cu refining. Parkes process exploits silver's higher solubility in zinc; cupellation oxidizes lead to litharge; Moebius is the silver-nitrate electrorefining analogue of Wohlwill.

geology: Native metal in oxidized zones of hydrothermal deposits; relatively minor compared with byproduct silver from base-metal ores.
extraction: Cyanidation then Merrill-Crowe to dore; cupellation and/or Moebius electrorefining to fine silver.
notes: Like gold, benefits from gravity recovery of coarse metal. Still frequently co-produced with base metals.

geology: Platinum arsenide; principal Pt mineral in Bushveld (Merensky/UG2) and Norilsk/Sudbury Ni-Cu sulfide ores. Associated with base-metal sulfides.
intermediate: Ni-Cu-PGM sulfide flotation concentrate; then PGM matte
extraction: Flotation (xanthate/dithiophosphate, pH 7.5-9) to Ni-Cu-PGM concentrate; smelt to PGM-rich matte; convert and base-metal leach to strip Ni/Cu/Co; pressure-oxidation leach of residue; solvent extraction + ion exchange + selective precipitation to separate the six PGMs; refine.
notes: Deepest refining chain in scope. PGMs are co-products, never recovered alone. Base metals (Ni/Cu/Co) stripped at the matte-leach stage cross-link to the base-metals catalog; arsenic is a sperrylite-specific byproduct.

geology: Platinum sulfide; abundant PGE sulfide in Bushveld Merensky/UG2 reefs alongside braggite and laurite.
intermediate: PGM-bearing sulfide concentrate; then PGM matte
extraction: Flotation with Ni-Cu sulfides; smelt to matte; base-metal removal; PGM refining via dissolution-precipitation, solvent extraction and ion exchange.
notes: Co-produced with all PGMs and base-metal sulfides; shares the Merensky/UG2 flotation-smelt-refine chain with braggite and sperrylite.

geology: Pt-Pd-Ni sulfide; major PGE sulfide of the Bushveld UG2 reef; carries significant palladium.
intermediate: PGM-bearing sulfide concentrate; then PGM matte
extraction: Flotation; smelt to matte; base-metal leach; solvent extraction / ion exchange / precipitation refining chain to separate Pt and Pd.
notes: Ni in the lattice ties it directly to the nickel base-metal circuit; main palladium-bearing primary PGM in UG2.

geology: Mercury(II) sulfide, the near-exclusive mercury ore; forms in low-temperature hydrothermal veins and hot-spring deposits, sometimes with stibnite.
extraction: Roasting/retorting at 500-600C: HgS + O2 yields Hg vapor + SO2; mercury vapor condensed on cooling and collected; distillation for final purity.
notes: Distinctive short chain: oxidative roast/retort volatilizes mercury, which is condensed. Rotary kilns/multiple-hearth furnaces for large tonnage, externally heated retorts for small/fine ore. Emits SO2; can co-occur with antimony (stibnite).
